Overview

Executive summary

SummaRace is an offline reading game for Grade 4 learners. For each story the learner reads it page by page, races to pick its story parts in a 3D runner, puts the parts in order, and then sums it up in 2–3 sentences, guided by Teacher Mira.

30stories in 10 sessions
5worlds, 6 levels each
4stages per level
0servers or accounts

What was built

Version 1.3.6 is a web game (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and three.js) inside a small Android app. It runs fully offline on Android 7.0 or newer. Learner progress is saved on the phone, and the teacher exports one CSV row per finished level for the research team. The summary is checked offline by rules (no AI model, no internet), and Teacher Mira speaks with 320 pre-recorded voice clips.

What this package contains

  • Chapters 1–7 describe the product (PRD), the technology (TRD), the screen flow, the system design, the look and feel, the data and the order in which it was built.
  • Chapter 8 lists what a laptop, PC or phone needs to run the game, with setup steps. Chapter 9 lists what is handed over and the items still open.
  • Appendix A lists every asset the game ships, with its source, author and license. Appendix B is the answer key for all 30 stories.

Status at handover

The game is feature-complete. Before it goes to learners, three things need attention (details in Chapter 9):

  1. Release 1.3.7 is signed with a new key, so every phone needs its records exported and the old app uninstalled first, and the release still needs a full play-through on a real phone.
  2. The music and all UI images (including Teacher Mira) have no recorded source, and some required credits (wordfreq, font licenses) are not yet in the game.
  3. The research team should confirm permission and credit lines for the stories, several of which are published children's books.
Chapter 1

Product Requirements

SummaRace v3 · version 1.3.6 · Android app com.summarace.app

1.1Overview

This document describes what SummaRace does, feature by feature, and how each feature is expected to behave. It covers the game as built in version 1.3.6, not planned features.

SummaRace is a reading game for Grade 4 learners. For each story the learner reads it page by page, races through its story parts in a 3D runner, puts the parts in order, and then sums it up in 2–3 sentences. The tagline on the title screen is "Read it · Race it · Sum it up!". Teacher Mira, a cartoon teacher, guides the learner with spoken lines the whole way.

1.2Product goal

Help Grade 4 learners practise reading comprehension and summarising with the Somebody – Wanted – But – So – Then (SWBST) method, in a game they want to keep playing, and give the teacher a record of every finished level that they can open in a spreadsheet.

The game has to work on low-cost Android phones in a classroom with no internet and no accounts.

1.3Users

Learner

A Grade 4 pupil. Types their name and section, plays the stories in order, earns stars and coins.

Teacher

Hands out the phones, reads the records screen, exports the CSV, can erase or bring back records.

Research team (client)

Wrote the 30 stories, questions and SWBST answers. Uses the CSV results for the study.

1.4Content scope

  • 30 stories in 10 sessions. Each session has one easy, one average and one hard story (levels 1–30).
  • Each story has 5 pages, 5 page questions (one per page), 1 main idea question, and 5 SWBST story parts with right and wrong answers.
  • The 30 levels sit in 5 worlds of 6 levels each: Sunny Meadow, River Bend, Story Town, Palm Beach and Summit Peak.
  • The pages, page questions, SWBST answers and main idea come word for word from the research team. The wrong answer choices, race wording and Teacher Mira's example summaries were written for the game.

1.5Features

Table 1.1 Features

FeatureDescriptionExpected behaviour
Title screenAnimated title with Teacher Mira, a PLAY button and Credits.PLAY opens "Who is playing?". Credits opens the credits popup.
Learner profilesName (required, max 40 characters) and section (optional, max 30).A new name and section makes a new profile on this device (matching ignores capital letters). Returning learners tap their name under "Or continue as". Progress is saved per profile.
World mapA scrolling path of 30 level nodes with a session bar (sessions 1–10) and a "go to my level" button.Levels unlock one by one. Tapping a locked level shows a card that sends the learner to their open level. Stars and best score show on finished levels.
ReadOne page at a time with a world picture, page dots and a Listen button.Mira says a short tip and then reads the page aloud with a recorded voice. "Answer the question" goes to that page's question.
Page questions3 answer choices in a new random order every time.A wrong answer is never revealed. After a wrong answer Mira offers "Read the story" or "Try again". After 2 wrong tries the story opens with the right part highlighted. Only a right first try counts for the score.
Main ideaAfter the last page, 4 choices: which one tells what the whole story is about.Same retry rules as page questions. Scored right or wrong on the first try.
RaceA 3D endless runner: the learner's runner (Max or Mia) escapes a police officer and dog.Each SWBST part becomes a question at the top with answers A, B and C shown in the 3 lanes. The learner swipes into the lane of the right answer and runs through its gate. Right = boost and the patrol falls back. Wrong = the patrol comes closer and the question comes back later. Trains and barriers must be dodged (swipe left/right, up to jump, down to roll). If the patrol catches the runner, the race restarts.
Story orderTap the 5 story parts into the Somebody, Wanted, But, So, Then slots.Right parts turn green and stay. After the first wrong check a 30-second clock starts (it pauses while the story or Settings is open). When time runs out Mira shows the right order and the level goes on. Score = parts right on the first check.
SummaryThe learner writes 2–3 sentences in English, in their own words.An offline checker gives feedback lines (see TRD). It passes when the summary names the main character, has most story parts and the main idea, and has no clear mistakes. After 3 tries Mira shows an example. After 4 tries the learner can choose "Finish, my teacher will check".
ResultsStars (1–3), a title, the score for each stage and coins earned.Total ≥ 85% = 3 stars "AMAZING!", ≥ 65% = 2 stars "GREAT JOB!", otherwise 1 star "GOOD TRY!". Buttons: Map, Replay, Next. The next level unlocks.
Teacher recordsA table of every finished level on this device.Copy CSV, Download CSV (saved to Download/SummaRace/ on Android), Share CSV (Android share sheet). "Erase all records" needs the word ERASE typed in; the last erase can be undone with "Bring back erased records".
SettingsTeacher voice, sound effects and music switches; Change player; Teacher records; Quit this story; Exit game.Switches are saved on the device. Quit is offered during a level, Exit game only inside the Android app.
Teacher MiraA guide docked at the bottom of every screen except the race and records.Speaks recorded lines and shows a speech bubble. The bubble folds away after 7 seconds, or after 2 seconds if it covers a button the learner needs. Tap her to hear the line again.
Android Back buttonHandled by the game, not the system.Closes a popup first. In the race, the first Back pauses. During a level it opens the Quit popup instead of dropping progress. On the map it goes back to the title screen.

1.6Scoring

The level total is the average of four stage scores:

Figure 1.1 Total score is the average of four parts

Coins collected in the race are added to the learner's coin total. A replay keeps the best stars and best score for that level.

1.7Constraints

  • Fully offline. No server, no login, no analytics, no ads. Everything ships inside the APK.
  • Android 7.0 or newer (minSdk 24), portrait only, phones with about 2 GB of RAM.
  • Records live only on the device they were made on. The teacher must collect the CSV from each phone.
  • The summary checker must run offline, so it uses word lists and rules, not an AI model.

1.8Out of scope

  • Syncing records between devices or to the cloud.
  • Teacher accounts, passwords or a class dashboard.
  • Languages other than English (the summary must be written in English).
  • iOS builds (the web game would run in a browser, but no iOS app is made).

Chapter 2

Technical Requirements

SummaRace v3 · version 1.3.6 (versionCode 17)

2.1Overview

This document lists the tools, technologies and structure used to build SummaRace v3, so anyone who picks up the code knows how it fits together and what it must keep doing.

SummaRace v3 is a web game (HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript, with three.js for the 3D race) that runs inside a small Android app. The Android app is a full-screen WebView plus a JavaScript bridge for things a web page cannot do on its own: the phone's voice, the clipboard, sharing, saving files and closing the app.

2.2Technical goals

  • Works with no internet. Every file is inside the APK. Nothing is fetched from the network.
  • Runs on low-cost phones. Android 7.0+ (API 24), about 2 GB RAM. The 3D models are not loaded at start-up (they preload in the background after the first tap), and GPU memory is freed after each obstacle.
  • Easy to change. No build step for the game. Stories are one data file. Opening the folder with a local web server runs the game in a desktop browser.
  • Safe for learners. No accounts, no tracking, no ads, no outside links during play.

2.3Technology stack

Table 2.1 Technology stack

AreaTool / technologyPurpose
Game UIHTML5, CSS, plain JavaScript (ES2018), one index.htmlEvery screen, popup, Teacher Mira, quiz, order and summary logic. No framework.
3D racethree.js r128 (three.min.js) + GLTFLoader.jsThe endless-runner race: toon shading, animated characters, trains, scenery.
3D modelsGLB files stored as base64 text in models/*.jsLoads from inside the app with no file-access problems. Compressed with glTF-Transform 4.1.1.
Sound effectsWeb Audio API, clips in assets.js as data URLsClick, coin, jump, bump, good, bad, win and so on.
MusicHTML Audio elements, looping MP3menu.mp3 on all screens, race.mp3 in the race. Ducks under Mira's voice.
Voice320 pre-recorded MP3 clips (Kokoro TTS) + voice/voice.js indexMira's lines and all 150 story pages read aloud. Falls back to Android TextToSpeech (en-US) or the browser's speech when a line has no clip.
Story datastories.js (global window.STORIES)30 stories with pages, questions, SWBST parts, main idea and model summary.
Word listwords.js (global window.SR_WORDS, 24,887 words)Checks that a summary is written in real English words.
StorageBrowser localStorage (inside the WebView)Profiles, progress, settings and the attempt log. See the Data Schema.
Android hostJava, one MainActivity, Android WebViewFull-screen portrait WebView, Back button, bridge window.SummaRaceApp.
BuildGradle, Android Gradle Plugin 8.7.3, compileSdk / targetSdk 35, minSdk 24Builds the APK. MP3 and WOFF2 files are stored uncompressed so the WebView can read them.
Version controlGit + GitHub (orbitsdev/summaracev3, public)Source, pull requests and history.

2.4Architecture

Figure 2.1 Architecture diagram

Script load order

three.min.js → GLTFLoader.js → assets.js → stories.js → words.js → voice/voice.js → the main script inside index.html. The main script is wrapped in one function (an IIFE), so its internals are not global. Each data file sets one global: SR_ASSETS, STORIES, SR_WORDS, SR_VOICE, SR_MODELS.

Main code modules inside index.html

Table 2.2 Main code modules inside index.html

ModuleWhat it does
StorageloadDb(), persist(), preferences. One JSON object under summarace.v1.
Teacher Mirasay() shows a line and speaks it. Picks a recorded clip by normalised text (vnorm), maps lines with names or numbers to a recorded version, avoids repeating the same line, and folds her bubble when it covers a button.
AudioSound effects on Web Audio, music on looping Audio elements, voice with two priorities (story reading is never cut off by a short line).
Screensshow(id) switches sections: learner, home, read, quiz, order, race, summary, result, records.
Level flowstartLevel → renderPage/askPage → askMain → startRace → startOrder → startSummary → finishLevel.
Summary checkerOffline rules, see section 6.
RaceA self-contained module (Race.prepare, Race.stop) with the three.js scene, worlds, characters, obstacles, gates, patrol and end scenes.
RecordsTable, CSV export (copy, download, share), erase with undo.

2.5Race engine

  • Three lanes at x = −2.2, 0 and 2.2. The runner (Max or Mia, chosen on the start card) is chased by an officer and a dog.
  • A gap meter (0–100) is the distance to the patrol. It starts at 60 and shrinks slowly while running, but not while the learner is reading a question. A right answer adds 24. A wrong answer, a train bump or a barrier hit takes 10–14 away, but these never push the gap below 8: only the slow drain can end the race. At 0 the runner is caught and the race restarts.
  • Each of the 5 SWBST parts is asked in turn. The question and the 3 answers show at the top. The game waits a reading time of 0.35 s per word (4–9 s, 25% less when a missed question comes back), then sends an answer gate down the track. The lane the runner is in at the gate is the answer.
  • Each level has its own seeded course (levelPlan(id)): speed, obstacle rows and spacing grow with the level number, so level 30 is harder than level 1 but each level plays the same every time.
  • Controls: swipe left/right to change lane, up to jump, down to roll. Tapping the left or right third of the screen also changes lane. Keyboard arrows (or A and D) and Space work in a desktop browser.
  • Race score for the level = share of the 5 parts answered right on the first try, kept across "Try the race again".

2.6Summary checker (offline)

Figure 2.2 Summary checker steps

The checker is rules-based by design, because it has to work offline on low-cost phones. It can miss things a teacher would notice, which is why the summary text and its status go into the CSV for the teacher to read.

2.7Performance and device rules

  • Start-up was measured at about 0.75 s with the CPU slowed 6× in a desktop browser. The 3D models (4.5 MB) are not part of start-up.
  • Obstacles and effects free their GPU geometry and materials when removed; shared models and textures are kept.
  • Portrait only. The layout uses safe-area insets for phones with a notch.
  • Hardware acceleration is on for the WebView.

2.8Build, run and release

Run in a browser:
  cd app/src/main/assets/www
  python -m http.server 8000      # then open http://localhost:8000

Build the APK:
  open the repo in Android Studio and build, or run: gradle assembleDebug
  the APK is written to app/build/outputs/apk/
  • Raise versionCode and versionName in app/build.gradle for every release. The next free versionCode is 18.
  • Release APKs are signed with the project's current signing key, which is kept off GitHub on the owner's PC. The original 1.2.0 key was lost, so phones with that old test build must uninstall it once.
  • Never commit the keystore, *.jks, *.keystore or local.properties. They are in .gitignore.

2.9Testing

  • Day-to-day testing is in a desktop browser at localhost:8000, with the phone size set in the browser's device mode.
  • Automated checks use Playwright with headless Chromium. Because the main code is private inside one function, tests reach it by injecting a small helper before the script ends.
  • An APK is built for a phone test only when a change is ready. Android-only features (voice fallback, Download folder on Android 7–9, Back button) must be checked on a real phone.
Chapter 3

App Flow

SummaRace v3 · version 1.3.6

3.1Overview

This document shows what happens when someone taps, and which screen comes next. It maps the main journeys through the game, from opening the app to finishing a level and exporting records.

3.2Key user journeys

First play

Open app → PLAY → type name and section → World map → Level 1 → read, race, order, summarise → Results → Next.

Returning learner

PLAY → tap the learner's name under "Or continue as" → the map scrolls to their open level → Play.

Replay for more stars

Map → tap a finished level → Play again. Best stars and best score are kept.

Teacher collects results

PLAY → Teacher records (or Settings → Teacher records) → Copy, Download or Share CSV.

Stop mid-level

Settings or the Back button → Quit this story → World map. The unfinished level is not recorded.

Change player

Settings → Change player (or tap the name chip) → "Who is playing?".

3.3App flow diagram

Figure 3.1 Main app flow from launch to results

3.4Inside one level

A level always runs in the same four steps, shown at the top of each screen as a step bar: Read & answer → Race → Story order → Summary.

Table 3.1 Inside one level

StepScreenWhat the learner doesWhat happens next
1ReadReads page 1 of 5 (Mira reads it aloud too). Taps "Answer the question".That page's question.
1Page questionPicks 1 of 3 answers.Right: "Next page" (or "Next: the main idea" after page 5). Wrong: Mira offers to show the story; after 2 wrong, the story opens with the part highlighted in yellow.
1Main ideaPicks 1 of 4 answers.Right: "Next: the race!".
2RaceStart card → Start running. Answers 5 story-part questions by lane.Mission complete → Continue.
3Story orderTaps the 5 parts into Somebody, Wanted, But, So, Then. Taps "Check order".All right: goes on by itself. Some wrong: green parts stay, 30-second clock, try again.
4SummaryWrites 2–3 sentences. Taps "Check my summary".Pass: "See my results". Not yet: feedback lines, try again.
—ResultsSees stars and scores.Map, Replay, or Next (hidden after level 30).

3.5Race flow

Figure 3.2 Race loop

3.6Unlock rules

  • A new profile starts with Level 1 open.
  • Finishing level n (any score) opens level n + 1. Levels open strictly one by one.
  • The session bar on the map groups levels in threes (session 1 = levels 1–3). A session chip is locked until its first level is open.
  • Level n belongs to world ⌊(n − 1) ÷ 6⌋: levels 1–6 Sunny Meadow, 7–12 River Bend, 13–18 Story Town, 19–24 Palm Beach, 25–30 Summit Peak. The world sets the race scenery and the screen backdrop.

3.7Back button

Table 3.2 Back button

WhereAndroid Back does
Any popup openCloses the popup.
Race, runningPauses the race.
Race, any card showingOpens the Quit popup.
Read, question, order, summary, resultsOpens the Quit popup (Quit this story / Exit game), so a mistap never loses the level.
World map or recordsBack to the title screen.
Title screenAndroid's normal Back (leaves the app).
Chapter 4

System Design

SummaRace v3 · version 1.3.6 (versionCode 17) · how the parts of the app fit together and why

4.1Overview

This document describes the system as a whole: who uses it, its components, how data moves between them, the main runtime sequences, and the design choices behind them. The TRD lists the tools; this document shows how they work together.

In short, SummaRace is a single-device, offline system. One Android app holds the game, the content and the saved data. The only data that leaves the phone is a CSV file the teacher exports.

4.2System context

Figure 4.1 System context diagram

4.3Components

Figure 4.2 Component diagram in layers

Table 4.1 Components

ComponentResponsibilityKey functions

Level flowRuns one level from first page to result and records it.startLevel, askPage, askMain, startRace, startOrder, startSummary, finishLevel
Race engine3D scene, course, patrol, answer gates, end scenes. Self-contained module with its own state.Race.prepare, Race.stop, Race.warm
Summary checkerOffline checks and feedback for the 2–3 sentence summary.checkSummary, scoreSummary, meaningChecks
Teacher Mira + VoiceShows and speaks lines, picks a recorded clip, never cuts off story reading.say, line, clipFor, playClip, speakRaw
Music + SFXLooping music with fades and ducking; sound effects from decoded clips or synthesised tones.Music.play/duck, sfx.*
Map + profilesWorld map, level cards, sign-in, unlocks, stars and coins.goHome, levelCard, learner form
RecordsTeacher table, CSV export, erase with undo.goRecords, csv, ERASE / restore
StorageOne JSON object in localStorage, read once, written after every change.loadDb, persist, savePref

4.4Data flow through one level

Figure 4.3 Sequence diagram for one level

4.5Teacher Mira's voice pipeline

Figure 4.4 Voice pipeline

4.6Race engine state machine

Figure 4.5 Race state machine

4.7Performance design

Table 4.2 Performance design

ProblemDesign choice
Slow start-up on cheap phonesNothing 3D loads at start-up. The 4.5 MB of models preload in the background 1.5 s after the learner's first tap (Race.warm), so they are usually ready before the first race.
Low frame rate in the raceThe first 2.5 s of a race are timed. Below 22 fps the game switches to low mode: no falling leaves, no sun shadows, less side scenery, pixel ratio 1. Pixel ratio is capped at 1.5 in any case.
Memory growing during a raceObstacles and effects free their GPU geometry, materials and textures when removed; shared models stay.
Loading files from inside the APK3D models and sound clips are base64 text inside .js files, so they load with a script tag even where file fetches are blocked.
Voice delayMira's clips are decoded once and cached in memory.

4.8Failure handling

Table 4.3 Failure handling

If this fails……the game does this
The race cannot start (no WebGL)Mira says the race could not start and the level continues to Story order with a race score of 50% and 0 coins.
A 3D model does not loadSimple shapes made in code stand in for the runner, patrol or trains.
A voice clip is missingThe phone's voice reads the line instead.
localStorage is blocked or fullEvery read and write is wrapped, so the game keeps running; progress is not kept.
Saving the CSV is not allowed (Android 7–9, permission refused)A copy is kept in the app's own folder and the button tells the teacher to use Share CSV.
Teacher erases by mistakeThe last erase is kept and can be brought back, merged with anything recorded since.

4.9Security and privacy

  • No network code, no analytics, no ads, no accounts. The app asks only for vibration and, on Android 7–9, storage (to save the CSV).
  • Learner data is a name, a section, scores and summaries, kept only on the phone in the app's private storage.
  • Teacher records have no password; ERASE needs a typed word, which guards against accidents, not against learners who deliberately look.
  • The repo is public, so the answer key and all content can be read by anyone. The signing key is kept off GitHub.

4.10Build and release pipeline

Figure 4.6 Build pipeline

4.11Design decisions

Table 4.4 Design decisions

DecisionWhyTrade-off
Web game in a WebView, not a native or Unity appOne code base that runs in a browser for fast testing; small APK (~13 MB); v1/v2 in Unity were heavier.Depends on the phone's WebView and WebGL.
No backendClassrooms may have no internet; no accounts or personal data on a server.Records stay per phone; the teacher must collect CSVs from each device.
Rules-based summary checkerWorks offline and gives the same result every time.Can miss meaning a teacher would catch; the text is saved for the teacher.
Recorded voice instead of live TTSA natural voice on any phone, no download.New lines need recording; the build script was lost.
One big index.html, no framework or build stepNothing to install; easy to recover and patch.A large file to read; modules are separated by comments, not files.
Answers in lanes, no pause (1.3.5+)Keeps the race moving, per the client's last request.Slow readers get 4–9 s of reading time before the gate; still worth a phone test with a slow reader.
Chapter 5

Design Brief

SummaRace v3 · version 1.3.6 · screenshots taken from main at phone size (390 × 844)

5.1Overview

This document sets the look of SummaRace: colours, fonts, components, and how each screen should look, so new screens match the ones already built.

5.2Brand identity

Bright, friendly, readable. A cartoon "sticker" world: white and cream cards with thick plum outlines on a bright sky. Big rounded buttons that look pressable. Teacher Mira is always nearby, so the learner never feels alone with a hard question.

For 9–10 year olds

Large text, large tap targets (answers are at least 58 px tall), one task per screen.

Reading first

Story text uses Andika, a font made for early readers. Game chrome never covers the story.

Kind feedback

Wrong answers shake and turn red, but the right answer is never given away. Mira always offers to show the story again.

Game energy

Stars, coins, medals, confetti and a chase scene make finishing a level feel like a win.

5.3Colour palette

Core

Plum#3a1460 · outlines, titles
Ink#2c1a4a · body text
Cream#fffaf0 · cards
Sky#2f8cf0 · background
Sun#ffd23f · stars, highlights
Go#22c06c · main buttons, right
Bad#ff4a3d · wrong, close

Story parts (SWBST)

Each story part keeps one colour everywhere: the race, story order and summary feedback.

Somebody#ff7a1a

The game has one bright look. It does not switch to a dark theme.

Headings are white with a thick plum outline on the sky, and plum on cards. Answer text is about 18 px (1.12 rem).

5.6Screens

Screenshots were taken in headless Chromium, so the 3D race uses software graphics and looks a little softer than on a phone.

5.7Worlds

Table 5.3 Worlds

WorldLevelsRace sceneryScreen backdrop
Sunny Meadow1–6Grass, flowers, houses, treesui/world-0.jpg
River Bend7–12River, houses, pines, mistui/world-1.jpg
Story Town13–18City buildings, treesui/world-2.jpg
Palm Beach19–24Sand, sea, palms, umbrellasui/world-3.jpg
Summit Peak25–30Snow, mountains, pinesui/world-4.jpg

The race sky cycles through 6 times of day (morning to sunset) by level, so neighbouring levels look different.

5.8Motion and sound

  • Buttons press down on tap. Right answers pop, wrong answers shake. Screens slide in. Confetti on the results screen for 4.5 s.
  • If the phone asks for reduced motion, all animations and confetti are turned off.
  • Short sound effects for taps, coins, right, wrong, jump, bump and win. Music lowers while Mira talks.
  • Voice, sound effects and music each have their own switch in Settings.

5.9Accessibility

  • Every icon button has a text label for screen readers. Mira's bubble is a live region, so her lines are read out.
  • Focus outlines are a thick pink ring.
  • Answer order is shuffled, so colour or position never tells the answer.
  • Every story page can be read aloud with the Listen button.
Chapter 6

Data Schema

SummaRace v3 · version 1.3.6 · this replaces a "backend schema": the game has no backend

6.1Overview

This document says where SummaRace's data lives, how it is structured, who can see it, and how the pieces connect.

There is no server and no database. Story content is a JavaScript file shipped in the app. Learner progress and results are saved in the phone's WebView storage (localStorage). The only way data leaves the phone is when the teacher copies, downloads or shares the CSV.

6.2Data model

Figure 6.1 Data model diagram

6.3Story content: stories.js

window.STORIES is an array of 30 objects, sorted by id when the game starts. Every story has 5 pages, 5 page questions with 3 options, a main idea question with 4 options, and 5 SWBST parts with 1 right and 2 wrong answers.

Table 6.1 Story content: stories.js

FieldTypeUsed for
idnumber 1–30Level number and unlock order.
daynumber 1–10Session number shown on screens ("Session 1 · Easy").
level"easy" | "average" | "hard"Difficulty tag and colour. Each session has one of each.
titlestringShown everywhere and copied into each record.
passagestringThe whole story in one piece. Used by the summary checker (copy check, names, vocabulary).
textstring[5]The 5 pages the learner reads.
quizQuestion[5]One question after each page. why is the page text that holds the answer; it is used to highlight the right part when the story is shown again.
mainIdeaQuestion (4 options)The main idea question after page 5, and the main idea check in the summary.
mainIdeaTextstringThe main idea in words; allowed vocabulary for the summary.
swbst{somebody, wanted, but, so, then}: StoryPartRace questions, story order items and summary scoring. words are the keywords that prove a summary told that part.
eventsstring[4]Allowed vocabulary for the summary checker.
modelSummarystringTeacher Mira's example, shown after the 3rd summary try and after a pass.
raceQuestion[6]Not used since 1.3.5. The old trivia race questions. The race now asks the 5 SWBST parts instead.
{
  "id": 1, "day": 1, "level": "easy", "title": "The Playground",
  "text": ["Molly and her friend Bella were playing at the playground. …", "…"],
  "quiz": [{ "q": "Who is the main character in the story?",
             "options": ["Bella", "Molly", "The teacher"], "answer": 1, "why": "…" }, …],
  "swbst": { "somebody": { "answer": "Molly", "wrong": ["Bella", "The teacher"],
                           "words": ["molly", "girl", "kid"] }, … },
  "modelSummary": "Molly wanted her turn on the swing, but Bella would not get off. …"
}

Other shipped data files

Table 6.2 Story fields in stories.js

FileGlobalShape
words.jsSR_WORDSOne string of 24,887 common English words separated by spaces.
voice/voice.jsSR_VOICEMap from normalised line text (lower case, letters and digits only) to a clip path, e.g. "please type your name first" → "voice/m-001.mp3". Story pages use the key "page <storyId> <page>". 170 Mira lines + 150 pages = 320 clips.
assets.jsSR_ASSETS{textures:{platformer}, models:{coin, cloud}, sounds:{bad, bump, click, coin, good, hit, jump, land, swish, tap, win}} as data URLs / base64.
models/*.jsSR_MODELSSR_MODELS[name] = "<base64 GLB>" for boy, girl, officer, city, suburb, trains, nature.

6.4Saved data: localStorage

Table 6.3 Other shipped data files

KeyValueWritten when
summarace.v1{profiles: {id: Profile}, current: id | null, log: Record[]}A learner signs in, finishes a level, or the teacher erases or restores.
summarace.v1.pref{voice: bool, sound: bool, music: bool} (all true by default)A switch in Settings changes.
summarace.v1.runner"boy" (Max) or "girl" (Mia)The runner is picked on the race start card.
summarace.v1.erasedA full copy of summarace.v1 from just before the last eraseThe teacher types ERASE. Removed again by "Bring back erased records", which merges it with anything recorded since.

An unfinished level is never saved: quitting mid-level leaves no record. If storage is blocked or full, the game keeps working for the session but nothing is kept.

6.5CSV export format

File name summarace-records-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, UTF-8 with a byte-order mark (so Excel opens it correctly), comma separated, one header row, then one row per finished level, oldest first. Values with a comma, quote or line break are wrapped in double quotes. The column order is fixed:

Table 6.4 Keys saved in localStorage

#ColumnTypeMeaning
1dateYYYY-MM-DDDate the level was finished (UTC date).
2timeHH:MMLocal time on the phone.
3learnertextName as typed.
4sectiontextSection or group as typed (may be empty).
5level1–30Story id.
6titletextStory title.
7key_details_pct0–100Page questions right on the first try.
8main_ideacorrect | wrongMain idea right on the first try.
9sequence_first_try_pct0–100Story parts in the right slot on the first "Check order".
10race_pct0–100Story parts answered right on the first try in the race.
11coinsnumberCoins picked up in the race.
12summary_pct0–100Story parts found in the passing summary, out of 5, minus half a part (10 points) for each wrong detail. 0 if handed to the teacher.
13summary_triesnumberScored summary checks (early checks like "too short" do not count).
14total_pct0–100Average of read & answer, race, order and summary.
15stars1–3Stars for this attempt (≥85 → 3, ≥65 → 2, else 1).
16minutesnumber, 1 decimalTime from opening the level to the result.
17summarytextThe learner's summary, word for word.
18summary_statuspassed | passed after example | teacher checkHow the summary step ended. Added in 1.3.2, kept as the last column so old sheets still line up.
date,time,learner,section,level,title,key_details_pct,main_idea,sequence_first_try_pct,race_pct,coins,summary_pct,summary_tries,total_pct,stars,minutes,summary,summary_status
2026-11-05,08:06,Juan Dela Cruz,Grade 4 - Sampaguita,1,The Playground,100,correct,80,100,24,100,1,95,3,6.4,"Molly wanted a turn on the swing, but Bella would not get off. …",passed

Column story_elements_first_try_pct existed before 1.3.3 and was a copy of race_pct. It was removed, so sheets from older builds have one more column.

6.6Access control

Table 6.5 CSV columns

WhoStory contentOwn progressOther learnersRecords / CSV
LearnerReadRead, add by playingSees names in "Or continue as"Can open Teacher records (no password)
TeacherRead—Sees all on the phoneCopy, download, share, erase (type ERASE), restore
Anyone with the APKRead (the files are inside the app; the repo is public)Nothing: data stays on each phone

There is no password on Teacher records. This was a choice for a classroom tool; the ERASE word and the undo protect against accidents, not against a learner who deliberately looks.

6.7Data storage

Where

WebView localStorage inside the app's private folder. Clearing the app's data or uninstalling deletes it.

Export

Android 10+: Download/SummaRace via MediaStore. Android 7–9: Download/SummaRace with storage permission. Or Share / Copy.

Backups

None automatic. The teacher should export the CSV after each session.

Personal data

Only the name and section typed in, and the summaries. Nothing is sent anywhere.

Chapter 8

System Requirements and Setup

SummaRace v3 · release 1.3.7 (versionCode 18) · what a laptop, PC or phone needs to run the game, and how to set it up

8.1Overview

SummaRace is made for Android phones, but the game itself is a web page, so it also runs on a laptop or desktop PC in a normal web browser. This document lists what each kind of device needs and gives the steps to get the game running.

Play on a laptop or PC

Open the game in Chrome or Edge. No install and no internet needed. Good for demos, panel defences and teachers checking the stories. See sections 2–4.

Play on an Android phone

Install the APK. This is how learners use it in class. See section 5.

Build a new version

For a developer changing the game: Android Studio, JDK 17 and the signing key. See section 6.

Figure 8.1 Three ways to run SummaRace

ItemMinimumRecommended

Tested on 11 November 2026: the full game (title, reading, questions, 3D race, story order, summary, results and records) runs in Chromium both straight from the folder (option A) and from a local server (option B).

8.3Install guide: play on a Windows laptop or PC

Each step says what to do, where to do it, the command to type (if any) and what you should see when it worked. Option A needs only a browser. Option B also needs Python.

  1. Check the browser Where: Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge (Edge is already on every Windows 10/11 PC). Type in the address bar: chrome://settings/help (Chrome) or edge://settings/help (Edge), then press Enter. You should see: "Chrome is up to date" or "Microsoft Edge is up to date" and a version number of 80 or higher. If Chrome is missing: download it from google.com/chrome.
  2. Turn on graphics acceleration (needed for the 3D race) Type in the address bar: chrome://settings/system or edge://settings/system Do: switch on Use graphics acceleration when available and click Relaunch if it asks.
  3. Download the game Where: in the browser, open github.com/orbitsdev/summaracev3/archive/refs/heads/main.zip (or open github.com/orbitsdev/summaracev3 and click the green Code button → Download ZIP). You should see: summaracev3-main.zip in your Downloads folder.
  4. Unzip it Where: File Explorer → Downloads. Right-click summaracev3-main.zip → Extract All… → choose a folder such as C:\Users\<you>\Documents → Extract. You should see: a folder Documents\summaracev3-main. The game itself is in summaracev3-main\app\src\main\assets\www (it contains index.html, stories.js and the models, voice and fonts folders).

Option A: open the game straight from the folder (no install)

  1. Open the game Where: File Explorer → summaracev3-main\app\src\main\assets\www Do: right-click index.html → Open with → Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. You should see: the SummaRace title screen with Teacher Mira and a green PLAY button. The address bar starts with file:///C:/.
  2. Go full screen with F11 (press F11 again to leave), then click PLAY.

Option B: run it from a local web server (for developers)

  1. Install Python 3 Download: python.org/downloads/windows → latest Python 3 Windows installer (64-bit). Do: run the installer and tick "Add python.exe to PATH" on the first screen, then Install Now.
  2. Check that Python works Where: press the Windows key, type cmd, press Enter (Command Prompt opens). Type: python --version You should see: Python 3.x.x. If it says "not recognized", see section 7.
  3. Open a Command Prompt inside the game folder Where: File Explorer → summaracev3-main\app\src\main\assets\www. Click the address bar at the top, type cmd and press Enter. You should see: a Command Prompt whose line ends with ...\app\src\main\assets\www>
  4. Start the server Type: python -m http.server 8000 You should see: a line like Serving HTTP on :: port 8000 .... Leave this window open while playing.
  5. Open the game Where: Chrome or Edge address bar. Type: http://localhost:8000 You should see: the title screen. To stop the server, click the Command Prompt window and press Ctrl + C, or close it.

Phone-sized view (optional)

In Chrome or Edge press F12, click the phone-and-tablet icon at the top left of the panel (or press Ctrl + Shift + M), pick a phone such as iPhone 12 Pro (390 × 844), then press F5 to reload.

8.4Playing on a laptop or PC

Table 8.2 Playing on a laptop or PC

ActionKeyboardMouse / touch
Change lane (pick an answer in the race)← → or A / DClick the left or right side of the track, or swipe
Jump↑, W or SpaceSwipe up
Roll↓ or SSwipe down
Close a popupEscThe close button

Differences from the phone app

  • Saved progress and records stay in that browser on that computer. Another browser, a private window, or "clear browsing data" starts empty. Option A and option B also keep separate records.
  • Records: use Download CSV (saved to the browser's Downloads folder) or Copy CSV. Share may not be offered on a PC.
  • Voice: Mira's recorded clips play as normal. The few lines without a clip use the computer's built-in voice.
  • Exit game is hidden; close the browser tab instead.
  • The browser may block sound until the first click. This is normal; sound starts after PLAY.

8.5Android phone requirements

Table 8.3 Android phone requirements

ItemRequirement
Android versionAndroid 7.0 (API 24) or newer; built for Android 15 (API 35)
MemoryAbout 2 GB RAM or more
StorageAbout 50 MB free for the app and its saved records
ScreenPortrait phone screen; phones with a notch are supported
InternetNot needed
PermissionsVibration; on Android 7–9 only, storage (to save the CSV to Download/SummaRace)

Before installing 1.3.7: export records, then uninstall the old app

Important. Version 1.3.7 (versionCode 18) is signed with a new key. It cannot update any earlier SummaRace on a phone: the 1.2.0 test build and every 1.3.x build, including 1.3.6, must be uninstalled first. Uninstalling deletes all learner progress and records on that phone, and the game cannot import them back. Do these steps on every phone first:

  1. Export the records Where: on the phone, open SummaRace → PLAY → Teacher records (or Settings → Teacher records). Do: tap Download CSV. Also tap Share CSV and send it to yourself (email or Drive) as a second copy. You should see: summarace-records-YYYY-MM-DD.csv in the phone's Download/SummaRace folder. Copy it to a PC before going on.
  2. Uninstall the old app Where: press and hold the SummaRace icon → App info (or Settings → Apps → SummaRace) → Uninstall → OK. Note: learners start again from level 1 in 1.3.7. Their earlier results stay only in the exported CSV.

Install the APK

  1. Copy the APK to the phone: connect the phone with a USB cable, choose File transfer on the phone, then in File Explorer drag app-release.apk into the phone's Download folder. (Google Drive or a messaging app also works.)
  2. Open it on the phone: Files app → Downloads → tap app-release.apk. When Android asks, allow Install unknown apps for the Files app, go back and tap Install.
  3. You should see: "App installed" and a SummaRace icon on the home screen. Open it and play the first page to check it works.

Git (optional)Anygit-scm.com/download/win, or use GitHub Desktop, or the ZIP from section 3.
PC8 GB RAM, about 10 GB free disk—
Signing keyThe SummaRace release key (.jks) and its passwordsThe new key made for 1.3.7 (11 November 2026), kept only on the owner's PC, never in the repository. Only needed to build a release APK, not to read these docs or play on a PC. To make a new one, see the end of this section.

There are two ways to build: Way 1, Android Studio (easier, but these steps have not yet been tested end to end on this project) and Way 2, the command line (tested: it built 1.3.7).

Way 1: build in Android Studio (not yet tested)

  1. Get the source code Either: download and unzip the ZIP as in section 3, steps 3–4. Or with Git: open Command Prompt in Documents\GitHub and type git clone https://github.com/orbitsdev/summaracev3.git You should see: a folder that contains settings.gradle, build.gradle and the app folder. This is the project folder.
  2. Install Android Studio Download: developer.android.com/studio → run the installer with the default options. First start: the Setup Wizard opens. Choose Standard, accept the licences and click Finish. It downloads the Android SDK (this takes a while).
  3. Install Android 15 (API 35) Where: Android Studio → Tools → SDK Manager (on the Welcome screen: More Actions → SDK Manager) → tab SDK Platforms. Do: tick Android 15.0 ("VanillaIceCream") API 35 → Apply → OK.
  4. Open the project Where: Android Studio → File → Open (Welcome screen: Open) → select the project folder from step 1 → OK. Choose Trust Project if asked. Wait: for the Gradle sync to finish (progress bar at the bottom right). Check View → Tool Windows → Build. You should see: BUILD SUCCESSFUL or "Gradle sync finished", and app in the Project panel on the left. If it says Gradle or the wrapper is missing: open File → Settings → Build, Execution, Deployment → Build Tools → Gradle, check Gradle JDK is 17 or newer, and accept Android Studio's offer to set up Gradle (8.9 or newer). Then File → Sync Project with Gradle Files.
  5. Raise the version number Where: Project panel → app → build.gradle (Module :app). Change: raise versionCode by 1 (after 1.3.7 / 18, the next is versionCode 19) and set versionName to the new version, e.g. '1.3.8'. Then click Sync Now at the top of the file.
  6. Test build (optional, not for learners) Where: Build → Build App Bundle(s) / APK(s) → Build APK(s). You should see: a pop-up "APK(s) generated successfully" with a locate link. The file is app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk. A debug APK cannot update the release app on the phones.
  7. Release build, signed with the SummaRace key Where: Build → Generate Signed App Bundle or APK… → choose APK → Next. Key store path: Choose existing… → the .jks file in Documents\SummaRace-signing → enter the key store password, key alias and key password → Next. Build variant: release → Create (Finish). You should see: "APK(s) generated successfully" → click locate. The file is app\release\app-release.apk in the project folder.
  8. Install it on a phone as in section 5, then play one full level before handing it out.

Never commit the keystore, *.jks, *.keystore or local.properties. The repository is public. A build signed with any other key cannot update the app already on the phones.

Way 2: build from the command line (tested)

Tested on 11 November 2026: version 1.3.7 (versionCode 18) was built this way on Windows with JDK 17, Android SDK Platform 35 and Gradle 8.14, with no Gradle wrapper.

  1. Install JDK 17 Download: adoptium.net → Temurin 17, Windows x64, .msi. In the installer, turn on Set JAVA_HOME and Add to PATH. Check in a new Command Prompt: java -version You should see: openjdk version "17.…"
  2. Get the Android SDK (Platform 35 and Build-Tools) Easiest: install Android Studio once (steps 2–3 of Way 1); it puts the SDK in C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Android\Sdk. In SDK Manager, tab SDK Tools, also tick Android SDK Build-Tools (35.x). Without Android Studio: download the Command line tools only ZIP from developer.android.com/studio, then run sdkmanager "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" You should see: folders Sdk\platforms\android-35 and Sdk\build-tools\35.0.0 (your Build-Tools number may differ; use the folder you have in the commands below).
  3. Tell the build where the SDK is Where: Windows key → type environment variables → Edit the system environment variables → Environment Variables… → under User variables click New. Add: name ANDROID_HOME, value C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Android\Sdk → OK. Open a new Command Prompt afterwards. Or: create local.properties in the project folder with the line sdk.dir=C\:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\Android\\Sdk. This file is in .gitignore; never commit it.
  4. Install Gradle 8.14 (the repository has no Gradle wrapper) Download: gradle.org/releases → v8.14 → binary-only. Unzip to C:\Gradle, so that C:\Gradle\gradle-8.14\bin exists. Add to PATH: in the same Environment Variables window, select Path → Edit → New → C:\Gradle\gradle-8.14\bin → OK. Check in a new Command Prompt: gradle --version You should see: Gradle 8.14 and a line with JVM 17.
  5. Raise the version number In app\build.gradle (any text editor), raise versionCode and versionName as in Way 1, step 5.
  6. Build the release APK (unsigned) Where: Command Prompt in the project folder (File Explorer → project folder → address bar → cmd → Enter). Type: gradle assembleRelease You should see: BUILD SUCCESSFUL and the file app\build\outputs\apk\release\app-release-unsigned.apk. The first build downloads the Android Gradle Plugin, so it needs internet and takes a few minutes.
  7. Align the APK (zipalign) Type (same window, one line): 
    "%ANDROID_HOME%\build-tools\35.0.0\zipalign.exe" -p -f 4 app\build\outputs\apk\release\app-release-unsigned.apk app-release-aligned.apk
    You should see: no error, and app-release-aligned.apk in the project folder.
  8. Sign it (apksigner) Type (one line; change the key path, alias and version to yours): 
    "%ANDROID_HOME%\build-tools\35.0.0\apksigner.bat" sign --ks "C:\Users\<you>\Documents\SummaRace-signing\summarace-release.jks" --ks-key-alias summarace --out SummaRace-1.3.7.apk app-release-aligned.apk
    Then: type the key store password when asked (nothing shows while typing; that is normal). You should see: SummaRace-1.3.7.apk in the project folder. This is the file to install on phones.
  9. Check the signature Type: "%ANDROID_HOME%\build-tools\35.0.0\apksigner.bat" verify --print-certs SummaRace-1.3.7.apk You should see: Signer #1 certificate DN: … with the names you gave the key, and no error.

Always zipalign before apksigner. Signing first and aligning afterwards breaks the signature.

Create a new signing key (only when the current key is not available)

Read this first. Android only lets an app update itself when the new APK is signed with the same key. An APK signed with a new key cannot update SummaRace already on a phone: the old app must be uninstalled first, and uninstalling deletes every learner's progress and records on that phone. Before switching keys, the teacher must Download CSV from Teacher records on every phone.

  1. Make a folder for the key, outside the project folder Where: File Explorer → Documents → right-click → New → Folder → name it SummaRace-signing. Why: anything inside the project folder can end up on GitHub by mistake.
  2. Easiest way: create the key in Android Studio Where: Build → Generate Signed App Bundle or APK… → APK → Next → under Key store path click Create new… Fill in: Key store path C:\Users\<you>\Documents\SummaRace-signing\summarace-release.jks, a password (twice), Alias summarace, a key password, Validity 25 years, and at least one name field (for example Organization) → OK. Then: continue with Way 1, step 7 (release → Create), or use the new .jks in Way 2, step 8.
  3. Or create it with a command (keytool) Where: Command Prompt opened in Documents\SummaRace-signing (address bar → cmd → Enter). Type (one line; keytool comes with Android Studio): 
    "C:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr\bin\keytool.exe" -genkeypair -v -keystore summarace-release.jks -alias summarace -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000
    Answer: the password questions and the name questions, then type yes to confirm. You should see: [Storing summarace-release.jks], and the file summarace-release.jks in the folder.
  4. Write down and back up Keep: the .jks file, the key store password, the alias (summarace) and the key password. Back up: copy the .jks to a USB drive and to private cloud storage. If it is lost again, every phone will need another uninstall.
  5. Never commit it Do not put *.jks, *.keystore, passwords or local.properties in the project folder or on GitHub; the repository is public. The project's build.gradle has no signing settings, so nothing in the code needs to change: the key is picked in the step 7 wizard each time.

8.7Troubleshooting

Table 8.5 Troubleshooting

ProblemFix
Blank or white pageUse Chrome or Edge, and check the whole www folder was copied (not only index.html). If it still fails, use option B.
"The race could not start"WebGL is off. In Chrome or Edge, turn on Settings → System → Use graphics acceleration, then restart the browser.
The race is slow or jerkyClose other tabs and plug in the laptop. The game switches to a lighter mode by itself below 22 frames per second.
No soundClick once on the page, check the volume, and check the Voice, Sound and Music switches in Settings.
Progress is goneThe browser's data was cleared, or a different browser, private window or option (A or B) is in use.
python is not recognisedInstall Python 3 from python.org and tick Add python.exe to PATH, or try py -m http.server 8000.
Port 8000 is busyUse another number, for example python -m http.server 8080 and open http://localhost:8080.

Reference

Glossary

APK
Android Package: the installable file of an Android app.
versionCode / versionName
Android version numbers. versionCode (17) must rise with every update; versionName (1.3.6) is the one people see.
WebView
The browser engine an Android app uses to show web pages. SummaRace runs inside one.
Bridge (SummaRaceApp)
The small set of Java functions the game can call: speak, stop, copy, share, save file and exit.
three.js
The JavaScript 3D library used for the race (release r128).
glTF / GLB
A standard file format for 3D models. The models are stored as GLB inside JavaScript files.
localStorage
Storage inside the WebView where the game saves profiles, progress and records.
CSV
Comma-separated values: the spreadsheet file the teacher exports.
SWBST
Somebody – Wanted – But – So – Then, the summarising method the game teaches.
Story parts
The five SWBST answers for a story, used in the race and in Story order.
Main idea
What the whole story is mostly about; one 4-choice question per story.
Session / Level / World
30 levels are grouped as 10 sessions of 3 (easy, average, hard) and 5 worlds of 6.
Teacher Mira
The cartoon teacher who guides the learner with speech bubbles and voice clips.
Patrol / gap meter
The officer and dog that chase the runner, and the 0–100 distance to them.
Answer gate
The row across the 3 lanes; the lane the runner is in at the gate is the answer.
TTS
Text-to-speech. Mira's clips were made with Kokoro TTS; lines without a clip use the phone's voice.
CC0
Creative Commons public domain dedication: free to use with no credit required.
CC BY / CC BY-SA
Creative Commons licenses that require credit (BY), and sharing changes under the same license (SA).
OFL
SIL Open Font License, used by most of the fonts.
PR
Pull request: a proposed change on GitHub, reviewed before it is merged into main.
Signing key
The private key that signs release APKs. Updates must use the same key.

A.2Gaps to fix before a public release

These are not guesses; each one is visible in the files.
  • Music and all UI images have no recorded source. The credits screen calls the music "original loops, made for this game" but there is no record of who made it or with what tool. The files carry a C2PA provenance tag from a file-handling tool, which only shows how they were copied, not who made them. The owner should confirm where Mira, the world pictures, the backdrop, stars, icons and both music loops came from.
  • wordfreq (CC BY-SA 4.0) is not credited on the credits screen. That license requires credit. Suggested credit: "Word list: wordfreq by Robyn Speer (CC BY-SA 4.0)".
  • The credits screen says "Full list in CREDITS.md", but that file was lost and is not in the app. It should point to this document, or a new credits file should be shipped.
  • The font license texts are not shipped. The SIL OFL and Apache 2.0 both ask for the license text to travel with the font files. Add OFL.txt and the Apache license next to fonts/.
  • Stories have no author credit. Several are published children's stories (for example "The Day the Crayons Quit" and "Owen and Mzee"). The research team should confirm they may be used and how to credit them.
  • Teacher Mira has no credit line on the credits screen, and no repo LICENSE says who owns the game code.

Lines that have no clip

All 80 lines in Mira's main line lists have clips. These fixed lines in the code do not, so they use the phone voice:

  • Time's up! Here is the right order. Read it once, then let's write your summary.
  • Last stage! Write 2 or 3 sentences that tell the story in your own words. Before you check, ask yourself: …
  • Tell me more! Write 2 or 3 sentences: who the story is about, what happened, and how it ended.
  • Some words are repeated too many times. Tell the story in sentences that make sense.
  • Write it in sentences, not a list of words. Use words like wanted, but, so, and then.
  • I see only one sentence. Please write 2 or 3 sentences, with a period at the end of each one.
  • Some details don't match the story. Look at the red lines and fix them.
  • Who is the story about? Name the main character in your summary.
  • Your summary needs the main idea. What is the whole story mostly about?
  • Good effort! Your teacher will read your summary and help you with it.

Lines built from a template (with a name, number or story title) were not checked one by one and may also fall back.

Appendix B

Answer Key

All 30 stories · built from stories.js on main (version 1.3.6)

B.1How to read this key

The game shuffles the answer choices every time, so the letter (A, B, C) changes from play to play. This key gives the answer text, not a letter.

  • Page questions: one per page, 3 choices. The right answer is in bold; the other two choices are listed after it.
  • Main idea: 4 choices, the right one is given.
  • Story parts (SWBST): the right answers are the same for the race (pick the lane) and for Story order (put them Somebody → Then). The 2 wrong race choices are listed after each.
  • Model summary: Teacher Mira's example, shown after the 3rd summary try. Any summary in the learner's own words that tells these parts passes; it does not have to match.

This key is in a public repository, by the owner's choice. Learners who find it could look up the answers.
